newsitem.title: UK: Tate and Lyle down as price worries persist.
newsitem.headline: Tate and Lyle down as price worries persist.

text.p: Shares in Tate and Lyle dropped to a seven-month low on Friday hit by expectations that pressure on U.S. sweetener prices would damage profits, dealers said.
By 1015 GMT, Tate and Lyle shares were 8-1/2p weaker at 441-1/2.
Dealers said bearish comments on the stock in the Daily Mail newspaper and talk that further broker downgrades could follow a NatWest downgrade earlier in the week had pushed the stock lower.
"NatWest were negative earlier in the week and it seems others may follow suit," one dealer said.
On Thursday, Tate and Lyle declined to comment on talk of pressure on the price of high fructose syrup, which accounts for some 60 percent of the output of its U.S. unit Staley.
Noting the talk of pressure on sweetener prices in a comment on the stock, the Daily Mail said: "Current year forecasts...definitely look too high. Avoid."
A report in U.S. trade magazine Milling & Baking News said last week: "High fructose prices appeared to be under extreme pressure as bookings for 1997 gained momentum."

The magazine added that pricing was said to have spanned a wide range but was "far lower than a year earlier and refiner predictions," and quoted one baker as saying: "I don't expect refiners to make money in 1997."
